newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PCI Leasing gets rousing welcome.
newsitem.headline: PCI Leasing gets rousing welcome.

text.p: PCI Leasing and Finance Inc got a warm welcome on its debut at the Philippine Stock Exchange on Monday and analysts said forthcoming initial public offerings this year would get a better reception compared to last year.

"We believe that IPOs this year will perform better than their counterparts (in 1996) due to better pricing and diversity in products," Urbancorp Securities Inc said in a research paper released on Monday.
PCI Leasing ended at 7.50 pesos, up seven percent from its offering price of 6.95.
The 121.2 million share IPO of PCI Leasing, a unit of Philippine Commercial International Bank, was oversubscribed.
The IPO accounted for 20 percent of the outstanding capital stock of the firm.
PCI Leasing shares were offered at price earnings multiple of 12.6 times its forecast 1997 earnings, Urbancorp said.

"Prospects for the company are bright because it is the biggest name in its category. It will grow in tandem with the economy because it caters to the financing needs of medium-sized enterprises," another broker said.
The Philippine economy is expected to grow by 7-8 percent this year against a forecast of over 7.0 percent in 1996.
PCI Leasing chief operating officer Rene Buenventura said his firm's 1996 net income is seen to reach around 255 million pesos from the year-ago 140 million.
"We expect to make around 255 million pesos in net income this year from gross revenues of 1.2 billion pesos," he told reporters.
"Our 1997 forecast is 330 million pesos from gross revenues of between 1.6 to 1.7 billion pesos," he said.
Buenventura said his firm planned to put up two additional branches yearly in the next five years as part of its expansion. The firm currently has eight branches in key cities nationwide.
PCI Leasing is expected to outperform the market with a projected growth rate of 30 percent this year as against the industry's 22 percent, he said.
Brokers said the good investor response to the PCI Leasing IPO set the tone for upcoming IPOs for the rest of the year.

About 10 companies have indicated their plans to be listed at the Philippine Stock Exchange this year. Among these companies, the market eagerly awaits the IPO of cellular phone operator Smart Communications Inc, a unit of Metro Pacific Corp, and Equitable Banking Corp.
Brokers said planned 1997 IPOs from the telecommunications, banking, retail and manufacturing industries, are expected to generate between 20 to 32 billion pesos.
Fourteen companies were listed in 1996 and raised a total of about 30.9 billion pesos, Urbancorp said.
IPOs in 1996 were priced at PE multiple of between 9.3 to 33.3 times their forecast earnings that year.
Out of the 14 IPOs, however, only five performed above their offering prices, Urbancorp said.
Brokers attributed the lacklustre performance of IPOs last year to the dearth of exciting issues. Only a few issues like Fortune Cement Corp, stirred the interest of foreign investors, they said.
